detours.why: D-666 ARM B: this B.Cu segment TERMINATES at the barrel (59.300,106.300) the same spec removes.  Relaying it between its own two ends asks the router to reach a site that is reserved and a bond that is gone; ARM A asked exactly that and got NO_PATH at 0.300 mm inside a 5.180 mm budget.  It is a stub of a removed bond, so it is REMOVED AND NOT PUT BACK and the gate's inert_removal_priced clause prices it.

note: D-666 ARM D -- the promotable shape. Same EIGHT units as arms A-C. The two signal detours RELAY (/IR_TX_GPIO16, /SX1262_CS_N); the GND stub is relay:false because it terminates at the barrel this spec removes. The per-site reserve DISCS of arms A/B are GONE and their job is done by a STATED LANE instead: reserve_corridor.py --lane along the route arm C proved (evidence/d666-wake-lane-guard.json, 3 corridors on F.Cu/B.Cu/In2.Cu, 93.561 mm, merged with the 49 pour-bond guards), passed to the gate as --guard. ARM C is why: with every relay OFF the gate's own route_join closes this edge in 35.342 mm / 5 vias, and with the /SX1262_CS_N relay ON it closes it in 148.213 mm -- the relay put the cut back in the same pocket it was bought out of. A disc reserves a via SITE; only a lane reserves the RUN between them.
